lines.text: Fifty summers ago. The pines are young, the hearthstone is clean, and the hands are yours, but younger.
You say it aloud, to nobody: "Three pines, a lake, and nobody. This'll do."

steps.objective: Take wood from the fallen pine: break its logs with the axe.
Lay the wood on the hearthstone: right-click it with the logs.
Light it: flint and steel on the wood.

lines.text: The fire takes. Out on the water, something moves under the still.

steps.objective: Catch a fish in the water with the rod.
Cook it on the fire: right-click the fire with the fish.

choices.reply: At first light you kick out the fire and shoulder your pack.

lines.text: The fish spits on the fire. A loon calls across the water, and nothing answers it.
You could stay. Nobody would know.

steps.objective: Choose: press its number.

done.text: One notch, for this summer. You walk on, whistling.

lines.text: Before you go, you look back at the middle pine.

steps.objective: Cut a notch in the middle pine: right-click its trunk with the axe.

mornings: Eat something before you go. Then go on; we'll follow.
Go. I'll keep the child from running after you.
agna.name: Agna
remarks: Eat something. You look like a ghost.
If it hurts, show me. If it doesn't, walk.
welcomes: Back in one piece. Sit, let me look at you.
There you are. Eat before you do anything else.

mornings: Go on ahead. I'll keep to the back, where I'm no trouble.
Mind the ridges today. Grey coats see a long way.
corin.name: Corin
remarks: I sleep with my boots on. Habit.

mornings: We'll be packing a while yet. Go on ahead.
Cart's loaded by noon. Walk on, we'll find your marks.
hob.name: Hob
remarks: Bring me that blade when it's dull.
Don't mind me. I think better with a hammer in my hand.
welcomes: You found us, then. Pot's on.

mornings: Can I walk with you today? ...Fine. Go on, then.
Tamsin says we're slow. Go on, we'll catch up!
pip.name: Pip
remarks: I practised walking quiet. Like you.
welcomes: You're back! What did you see?
I watched for you all day!

cold: She turns her back on you.
rue.name: Rue
remarks: Mud and water, light-bearer. That's all there is out here.

cold: She spits in the water and won't look at you.
sedge.name: Sedge
remarks: Mind where you put your feet. The bog keeps what it gets.

mornings: We're packing up. Go on ahead; we'll follow your marks.
Don't wait for us. Look for our smoke tonight.
tamsin.name: Tamsin
remarks: We follow your marks. Don't make me regret it.
The bell's still with us. So are we.
welcomes: There you are. Sit, and tell me what's ahead.

cold: She won't meet your eyes. Maybe she's afraid to.
tansy.name: Tansy
remarks: Don't look at me like that. I saw what I saw.

reward.claimed: You take up his pack: a tent, a bed, a little food, and room for everything else.
reward.text: a backpack, a tent, a bed and a little food.
reward.title: His Pack

choices.reply: Nobody, now. A man who walked too little and stopped too long.
By my fire. Off the road, where nobody comes.
I was going to ask you that.

lines.text: You wake on cold ground beside a fire. You don't remember lying down. You don't remember anything before this fire.
An old man sits across the flames, propped against a log. His face is grey, and his breath rattles.
There you are. Thought I'd go before you woke.

steps.objective: Sit with the stranger.

people.stranger: An old man who found me by the road and brought me to his fire. He was dying.

story: I woke by a stranger's fire. I don't know my name, or how I came to be there.

choices.reply: Better than you'd like. Don't ask me how. There isn't time.
Good. Names are for people who stay.
choices.text: I don't know my own name.

lines.text: I found you lying by the road and brought you here. It took the last of what I had.
Don't look at me like that. I'm dying, that's all. I'm old, and I walked further than I had left in me.
His shirt is open at the collar. An old white scar runs across his chest, over the heart.
Let me look at you. ...Yes. It's you, then.

steps.objective: Sit with the stranger.

people.stranger: He said bringing me to his fire took the last of his strength. He knew my face, and wouldn't say how. An old white scar ran over his heart.

choices.reply: That's all I need.
choices.story: I told him I'd carry it.

choices.reply: Nobody does, at first. Carry it anyway.
choices.story: I told him I didn't even know who I was. He said to carry it anyway.
choices.text: I don't even know who I am.

lines.text: He fumbles at his belt and holds out a closed fist. It shakes.
Hold out your hand.
He presses something into your palm: a coal no bigger than a thumb, grey and cold as a stone.
That's an ember. Mine. It's been cold for years.
Walk with it and it wakes. It lives on what you see: new ground, every day.
Three things, and I won't have the breath to say them twice.
Walk every day. A cold ember is no use to anyone.
Never stay long in one place. Stay, and something finds you.
And never sleep in the open. A tent, with a fire by it. Sleep in the open and something comes to look.

steps.objective: Sit with the stranger.
story: He gave me his ember, cold as a stone, and told me to walk with it.
He gave me three rules: walk every day, never stay long in one place, and never sleep in the open, only in a tent with a fire by it.

words.ember: What the stranger gave me: an ember, a coal no bigger than a thumb, cold as a stone. He said it wakes if I walk with it, and that it lives on what I see.

lines.text: He coughs for a long time. When he looks up, he looks past you, at something that isn't there.
Don't let it... the shards. I took them. Don't let it have...
He doesn't finish. His hand goes slack, and his head drops to his chest.

steps.objective: Sit with the stranger.

people.stranger: He died before I learned his name.

story: He died before he could finish: "Don't let it... the shards. I took them. Don't let it have..." I don't know what he meant.

words.shards: He said he took them, and not to let "it" have them. I don't know what they are, or what "it" is.

burial.text: You dig beside his fire until your hands are raw, and lay him in. At the head of the grave you raise a stone.
It's blank. You never learned his name.
What do you write on his stone?

choices.reply: You scratch the words into the stone.
choices.stone: Here rests a good man, who gave all he had.
choices.text: Here rests a good man, who gave all he had.

choices.reply: You scratch the words into the stone.
You scratch the words into the stone.
You leave the stone as it is.

done.text: You stand at the grave a while. His fire is burning low. He said not to stay.
His pack lies by the fire. He won't need it now.

lines.text: The fire pops. The old man is dead.
You can't leave him here for the crows.

steps.objective: Bury him.
story: I buried him by his fire. On his stone I wrote: "{stone}"
steps.unwritten: I buried him by his fire, and left his stone bare. I didn't know what to write.

quests.summary: I woke by a stranger's fire with no name and no memory of the road. He is dying, and he wants to talk.
quests.title: The Last Fire

done.text: The land here is new to you. The coal in your hand is a little less cold.

lines.text: He knew your face. You don't. All he left you is a cold coal and three rules.
It wakes on new ground, he said. Maybe it remembers what you can't.

steps.objective: Find new ground for the ember: {left} blocks to go.
story: I walked away from his fire. He knew who I was, and the ember is all I have of that, so I took it somewhere new.

lines.text: The sun is getting low. His last rule comes back to you: never sleep in the open. A tent, with a fire by it.

steps.objective: Pitch your tent, light a campfire beside it, and rest by the fire.
story: I made my first camp: my tent, and a fire beside it.

done.text: The ember in your hand grows warm. Then, for the first time, it glows.
Over the ridge ahead, smoke. Under it, the sky is red.
The ember leans in your palm, the way a needle leans, towards the smoke.

lines.text: You sit by your fire. The shadows stretch, and the sky goes gold, then red.

steps.objective: Rest by your fire.
story: At dusk the ember woke in my hand. It had seen new land, the way he said it would.
Then I saw the smoke over the ridge.

words.ember: It woke on my first evening on the road. It's warm now, it glows, and it leans towards where I'm meant to go.

quests.summary: He knew my face, and the ember might know the rest. Take it to new ground, and make a camp of my own before dark.
quests.title: The First Day

steps.awake: Not tonight. The sky over the ridge is red.

done.text: The town burns. Roofs have fallen in, and nothing moves but the fire.

steps.objective: Go to the burning town, tonight.

steps.awake: Not here. Not among the dead.

clues.text: A man by the well. His shirt is torn open over the heart. His purse is still on his belt.
A woman in a doorway, opened the same way. Her rings are still on her hands.
A strongbox stands open in the inn, full of emeralds. Nobody took a single one.
Tracks of many feet, out of the dark and back into it. None of them carried anything away.
The bell tower stands, black but whole. Under it, behind a cellar door, someone is crying.

lines.text: In the smoke, the ember throbs in your fist, as if it wants to be held up.

steps.objective: Find {needed} signs of what happened here. ({found}/{needed})

agna: Not now. Listen. Are they gone?
hob: One more step and I'll swing.

story: Whatever came to the town wasn't after plunder. It opened people over the heart, and left their purses.

words.ember: Held up, it shows me for a moment what has passed by.

steps.awake: Not now. Someone is crying under the bell tower.

choices.reply: Mam said Wayfarers aren't real.
choices.story: I told Pip I don't know what I am.
choices.text: I don't know what I am.

choices.reply: Mam said Wayfarers aren't real.
choices.story: I told Pip I suppose I am one.

lines.text: Behind the cellar door, four faces in the light of a small fire.
Stay back! ...It's a person. It's only a person.
I'm Agna. I mend people, when there's anything left to mend. That's Hob, our smith.
You've seen them out there. They never take anything. They only open the chest.
Tamsin. I was Tollbridge's elder. It stood three hundred years. One night.
I'm Pip. You've got fire in your hand. Like in the stories. Are you a Wayfarer?

steps.objective: Go down into the cellar.

people.agna: The healer of Tollbridge. She showed me the dead: they never take anything, she said, they only open the chest.
people.hob: The smith of Tollbridge, big and frightened, and the first to see I was only a person.
people.pip: A child of Tollbridge. Pip's mother died the night it burned. Pip thinks I'm a Wayfarer out of the old stories.
people.tamsin: The elder of Tollbridge. Her town stood three hundred years, she says, and fell in one night.

story: Four of them were alive, in the cellar under the bell tower: Tamsin, their elder; Agna, the healer; Hob, the smith; and a child, Pip.

words.tollbridge: Tamsin's town, at a river crossing. It stood three hundred years and burned in one night.
words.wayfarer: Pip's word for me. In the stories Tollbridge told its children, Wayfarers carried fire and never stayed anywhere.

steps.awake: Not yet. Sit with them by their fire first.

lines.text: Pip. Come here. ...Sit down, you. You're shaking.
Here. I made it for a man who won't be fetching it now.

steps.objective: Rest by their fire.

people.hob: He gave me a blade he made for a man who didn't live to fetch it.

agna: Warm your hands first. Talk after.
Pip, sit still. Let them be.
hob: Three hundred years of iron in my forge, and all I saved is a hammer.
pip: Is it warm? The fire in your hand? Can I hold it?
Mam used to sing at the fire.
tamsin: Sit, if you're staying. We've nothing to give you but the fire.

reward.claimed: Hob's blade is plain and heavy, and sharper than it looks.
reward.text: made for a man who didn't live to fetch it.
reward.title: Hob's Blade

steps.awake: Not with them at the door.
steps.failed: The door gives way, and everything goes dark.

lines.text: Outside, something scrapes at the stones. Then more of them.
They never come back. What did you bring?
Hold the door!

steps.objective: Hold the cellar door until morning.

people.tamsin: She asked what I brought with me when they came back. I think she meant the ember.

agna: Keep them off the door. I can't mend what they open.
hob: I've got the door. You get the ones that come round.
Hold! It's oak. It'll take it if we do.
pip: Are they going to come in?
tamsin: The stone will hold. Make sure the door does.
They never came back before. Never.

steps.retry: Try the night again from the cellar
story: They came back in the night, for the cellar. Tamsin thinks they came for me. We held the door until morning.

done.text: The last of them falls back into the dark. The sky greys, and then it is morning.
What is left of them crumbles in the sun.

steps.objective: Hold the cellar door until morning.

agna: Nobody's bleeding who wasn't. That's a good night, now.
pip: Is it over? Is it morning?

choices.reply: It rang for every child born in Tollbridge. It comes. Hob, the cart.
choices.story: I told her to leave the bell. She's bringing it anyway.

choices.reply: Thank you. Hob, the cart.
choices.story: I told her we'd take the bell.

lines.text: You carry fire. In the stories, a Wayfarer can feel the way. Lead us somewhere they can't find us.
We'll follow you. Whatever you are.
Tamsin sits by the town's bell, fallen from its tower and black with smoke.
The bell comes with us.

steps.objective: Talk to Tamsin.

people.agna: She took Pip in, the morning after.

agna: Talk to Tamsin. She won't go anywhere without it.
hob: If she says the bell comes, the bell comes. I'll find a cart.
pip: The bell rang when I was born. Tamsin says it rang for everyone.

story: At dawn they asked me to lead them. I don't know where to. Tamsin won't go anywhere without her town's bell.

lines.text: Go on ahead. We'll be by water before dark. Look for our smoke.

steps.objective: Make for their smoke.

agna: Sit. The rest of the day can pass without you.
hob: The cart held. That bell's heavier than it looks.
pip: We made a camp! A real one, like the Wayfarers in the stories.
tamsin: Sit by the fire. You've walked enough for one day.

choices.reply: One day. I'll hold you to it.
choices.story: Pip asked me to teach the way of a Wayfarer. I said one day.

choices.reply: I know. I was there.
choices.story: Pip asked me to teach the way of a Wayfarer. I said it isn't like the stories.

lines.text: You walk ahead. We'll follow your marks.
Give me that arm. You've been bleeding since the door.
She binds the cut, and keeps two fingers on your wrist a moment too long.
Slow. Like something asleep. Well. You've had a night.
That blade's yours now. When it's dull you bring it to me. Don't you dare throw it away.
And take these. My patterns. Copper and iron want shaping, not just hammering.
Will you teach me? To be a Wayfarer?

steps.objective: Sit at the caravan's fire.

people.agna: At the fire she held my wrist too long, and said my heart was slow, like something asleep.
people.tamsin: She made me their scout: I walk ahead, and they follow my marks.

reward.claimed: You take Hob's patterns: one for every tool he makes, and one for its rod.
reward.text: his patterns for tools, from his own bench.
reward.title: Hob's Patterns

story: They made camp by water, and I found their smoke. Tamsin says I'm their scout now: I walk ahead, and they follow my marks.

done.text: The fire burns low. Around it, the last of Tollbridge sleeps.

steps.objective: Sleep in your tent by their fire.

agna: Get in your tent. I'll see to the fire.
hob: Go on. I'll sit up a while.
tamsin: Sleep. Someone has to walk ahead tomorrow.

quests.summary: Something is burning over the ridge, a whole town of it. Go and see.
quests.title: Ash

done.text: Under the trees, a mouth in the hillside, framed in old timber. Old rails run out of it into the grass, broken in places, past a heap of spoil.
The pull comes from below now.

lines.text: Agna asked you to lead them somewhere they can't be found. You don't know where that is.
The ember tugs at your hand, the way it leaned towards the smoke over Tollbridge. This time there is no smoke.
Somewhere far ahead, something is calling it. Maybe it knows.

steps.objective: Follow the pull: walk where the ember flares.
story: The morning after the caravan's first fire, the ember pulled for the first time, towards something far ahead.

words.ember: It pulls towards something it wants. Held up, it flares when I face the way.

done.text: The drift opens into a hall, cut square and high. On a stone at its far end, something hums.

lines.text: Cold air breathes out of the dark. Someone dug this a long time ago, and went a long way down.

steps.objective: Go down into the old tunnels, where the ember pulls.
story: It led me to old tunnels under a forest, and down.

done.text: A warmth runs up your arm, and then a voice you last heard dying:
Well. That's one.
Don't look so surprised. Did you think I'd let you carry it alone?
You heard me at the fire. The shards. Gather them, bring them to a frame, and we put its eye out for good.
A frame. You'll know one when you see it. No more burning towns.
When you look down, old tracks stand out on the ground, as if the ember held them up for you.

lines.text: On the stone lies a sliver of something like dark glass. It hums, and the ember in your hand hums back.

steps.objective: Take it from the stone: right-click it.

people.stranger: His voice came back with the first shard. Nobody else hears it. He wants the shards brought to a frame, to put out "its eye".

story: In a hall at the bottom of the tunnels lay a shard. When I took it, it sank into the ember, and the stranger spoke to me. He's dead. I heard him anyway.

words.shards: The first lay on a stone in a hall under the forest, humming. It sank into the ember, and his voice came with it.

lines.text: Go on, back to your caravan. Don't mind me. I'll be quiet. Mostly.

steps.objective: Make for their smoke.

lines.text: You came back different. What's in that hand now?
She can't hear me. Only you can.
The ember was mine once. Now it's yours, and it seems I came with it.
I made my first camp by a lake, under three pines. It's to the {direction} of here. I'd like to see it again.

steps.objective: Sit with Tamsin at the caravan's fire.
story: At the caravan's fire his voice told me where he made his first camp: by a lake, under three pines, to the {direction}. He wants to see it again.

quests.summary: The ember pulls towards something far ahead, and it won't say where. Hold it up, turn until it flares, and walk that way.
quests.title: The Pull

done.text: Three pines over still water. Under them, a ring of stones gone green, and the bones of a lean-to.
Three pines. They were smaller.

steps.objective: Find his first camp, by a lake under three pines.
story: He led me to a lake under three pines, where he made his first camp.

clues.text: Notches cut into the middle pine, one above the next, the oldest grown over with bark. Somebody came back here, summer after summer.
A stake at the water's edge, a rotten line still knotted round it. Somebody fished here.
A flat hearthstone in the ring, black with old fires. Cut into it, long after the soot, is an open eye.

done.text: That stone. Touch it. I want to see it the way it was.

lines.text: Whoever sat here, sat here often. Hold up the ember: it shows what he left.

steps.objective: Look at what he left, with the ember held up: {found}/{needed}.

done.text: You stand at the hearthstone again. The eye is cut into it, as before.
I was happy here.
...Wait. That sack wasn't there.

steps.objective: Touch the hearthstone: right-click it.

people.stranger: He was young once, and happy. At his first camp I made camp as him, and I wanted to stay. He walked on.

story: When I touched the hearthstone, the ember flared, and I was him, young, making camp under three young pines. I wanted to stay one more summer. He didn't.

clues.text: A sack, dry, as if it was set down days ago. Inside: bread, dried fish, and a folded note.

done.text: The note: "For whoever carries his light now. Eat. - M."
...Someone's been here. Someone who knows my camps.

steps.objective: Look in the sack under the lean-to: right-click it.

reward.claimed: You pack the bread and the fish, and keep the note.
reward.text: bread, dried fish, and a note signed M.
reward.title: Under the Lean-to

story: Under his lean-to someone had left bread, dried fish and a note signed M. Somebody knew I'd come.

lines.text: Back to the caravan. I've seen what I wanted to see.

steps.objective: Make for their smoke.

quests.summary: The voice wants to see the camp he made when he first set out, by a lake under three pines. Find it.
quests.title: His First Camp

steps.objective: Watch the road for whatever M. leaves next.
story: Someone signing themselves M. leaves food where he used to camp. They knew I would come.

quests.summary: Someone left food under his lean-to, with a note signed M. They know his camps, and they know someone carries his light now.
quests.title: The Gifts

done.text: A horn sounds across the water, low and long.

lines.text: The ember tugs at your hand again: steady, patient, towards something a long way off.

steps.objective: Follow the pull: walk where the ember flares.
story: The morning after his first camp, the ember pulled again, towards something far ahead.

done.text: Across the water a horn calls twice. The last of the men in grey turn and climb back towards the hill.

steps.failed: The wounded man goes down in the shallows, and doesn't get up.

There! The ember! Take them both!
Fight or run. Don't just stand there.

steps.objective: Keep the wounded man alive while they come across the ford.

corin: Keep them in the water. They're slow in the water.
I can't stand. Don't let them reach me.

story: At a river ford, men in grey came across the water after a wounded man, and after the ember. We held the bank.
steps.wave: They come across the ford: {wave} of {waves}

choices.reply: Thank you. I mean it. I'll keep up, or I'll keep quiet.
choices.text: Come with us. You won't get far alone.

choices.reply: I've kept up with worse than you. Lead on.

lines.text: They'll be back with more. They always come back with more.
Let me see your hand. ...That light.
I know that light. I'd know it anywhere.
Corin. Don't thank me. I brought them.
They're Gazebound. My own company, until last night.
Their heir wants that coal more than he wants me. And he wants me badly.
He pulls his shirt open. Over his heart runs an old white scar, like the one on the old man by the fire.
We all carry one. They let the night look into you. If you live, it never looks again.
The man who carried that light before you. I served under him, six winters.
Don't ask me his name. Not yet.
Where are you walking? Can a man with one good leg walk with you?

steps.objective: Talk to the wounded man by the ford.

people.corin: A deserter from the men in grey, with their scar over his heart. He served under the stranger for six winters, and won't say his name. We held the ford for him.

story: The man was Corin, a deserter. He knew the ember's light, and the man who carried it before me, and he wouldn't say his name. He walks with us now.

words.gazebound: Men in grey who hunt whoever carries an ember. Every one of them has a scar over the heart, as the stranger had. Corin was one of them.
words.heir: Whoever leads the Gazebound. Corin says he wants the ember more than anything, and Corin ran from him.

lines.text: Go on ahead. I'll follow your smoke. I'm good at following smoke.

steps.objective: Make for their smoke.

Not one of them. Not any more.
The man who had that ember before you. Where is he?

steps.objective: Wait for Corin's word: he'll say when you're ready.
story: Corin's brother took the Gazebound's scar the same night Corin did, and still serves at the outpost above the ford. Corin will say when.

quests.summary: Corin's brother serves the Gazebound at the outpost above the ford. Corin will say when the team is strong enough to fetch him.

...Not his, then. Whatever you are.
Go down, if it wants you. Under the water, where it shows you no face.
Drink this first, or the bog keeps you.

forced.text: Something foul splashes over you. Your arms and legs go heavy.

lines.text: That's far enough. We know that light.

steps.objective: Talk to the old woman on the porch.

people.rue: The eldest of three witches who keep a hut over a black pool. She curses the man who carried this ember before me: he swore by it, and broke his word.
people.sedge: The second of the witches, hard as a root. The man who carried this ember cost them two huts, and she hasn't forgiven it.
people.tansy: The youngest of the witches. She looked into my eyes and flinched. Something looks out of me, she said.

rue: Go down, or go home. Don't stand on my porch.
sedge: Mind where you put your feet. The bog keeps what it gets.
tansy: Don't look at me like that. I saw what I saw.

reward.claimed: You tuck the bottle away. It smells of the swamp.
reward.text: A stoppered bottle that smells of the swamp. Drink it before you go under, and the water lets you breathe a while.
reward.title: The witches' brew

story: In a swamp the ember led me to three witches at a black pool. They know this light, and hate the man who carried it. The youngest looked into me and flinched, and they let me go down.

words.marsh_mothers: Whoever kept the black pool before the witches. The witches keep it now, and won't say what lies under it.

done.text: You come up out of black water into air that smells of earth: a hall, dry, sunk in the mud. On a stone at its heart something hums.

lines.text: Witches. They'd curse the rain for falling. Go on, then. Down you go.

steps.objective: Drink the brew, then go down into the black pool and follow the ember.

rue: You've had your leave. Go down.
sedge: Mind where you put your feet. The bog keeps what it gets.
tansy: Hold the light up when you're under. It knows the way better than you do.

story: Under the black pool a drowned tunnel led to a dry hall, sunk in the mud.

asking.text: The shard hums on its stone. Up on the porch the fisher is sitting up, because of whatever hums down here.

choices.reply: You close your hand on it.
You leave it humming on its stone.

reward.claimed: You stow the bottles. They're warm.
reward.text: Two of the witches' bottles, brewed from the black water. Drink one when a wound won't close.
reward.title: The witches' brews

closes.the_witches_debt: The black pool is only water now. There was nothing left to brew with, and the fisher's fever was his own to fight.

lines.text: On the stone lies a sliver like the first, humming, and the ember hums back.

steps.objective: Take it from the stone: right-click it.
story: In the hall under the black pool lay a second shard.

words.shards: The second lay on a stone in a hall under a black pool in the swamp, where the witches keep their hut.

done.text: The stair ends behind a wall that is no wall, in a cellar of roots. A ladder, a hatch, and you come up into a room that smells of smoke.
All these years we kept the door, and never knew it.
And the pool's gone flat as rain water. Whatever you took, it was ours.

lines.text: Two. They'd have sat on it forever, brewing over it.
Beside the stone, a stretch of mud wall goes faint as smoke. Behind it, steps climb into the dark.

steps.objective: Go up the stair behind the faint wall.
story: Taking the shard showed me a wall that was no wall: the Marsh Mothers' own stair, up into the witches' cellar. Their pool has been plain water since.

words.true_sight: Since the second shard I see through what isn't there: a wall that's only seeming shows faint as smoke.

done.text: The stair ends behind a wall that is no wall, in a cellar of roots. A ladder, a hatch, and you come up into a room that smells of smoke.
All these years we kept the door, and never knew it.
You paid his debt and took our water. Then we're even, you and I.

lines.text: Two. They'd have sat on it forever, brewing over it.
Beside the stone, a stretch of mud wall goes faint as smoke. Behind it, steps climb into the dark.

steps.objective: Go up the stair behind the faint wall.
story: I took the shard, knowing what it cost the witches. It showed me the Marsh Mothers' own stair, up into their cellar.

words.true_sight: Since the second shard I see through what isn't there: a wall that's only seeming shows faint as smoke.

done.text: You left it.
Then the water's still ours, and so's our door, light-bearer, whenever you need it.

lines.text: Soft. That's one fewer at the gate.

steps.objective: Swim back up through the black pool.
story: I left the shard on its stone, for the witches' cups. The stranger called it soft.

lines.text: Back to your caravan. Mind the bog on the way out.

steps.objective: Make for their smoke.

quests.summary: The ember pulls on, the way it pulled before the horn at the ford. Hold it up, turn until it flares, and walk that way.
quests.title: Still Water

clues.text: A blue orchid on the bank, the one Rue wanted.
Frogspawn at the water's edge, cold and quick.
A worn step at the pool's edge, where they dip their bottles. You fill one with black water.

lines.text: That man came up our water two days ago, burning. We've nothing left to brew with.
A blue orchid, frogspawn, and a bottle of the black water. My knees won't take me round the pool any more.
The one who carried that light owes us. You can pay some of it.

steps.objective: Find what the brew needs round the pool: a blue orchid, frogspawn and the black water.

people.fisher: A fisher from somewhere downriver, burning with fever on the witches' porch.

story: A fisher lay fevered on the witches' porch. Rue sent me round the pool for what their brew needs.

lines.text: Rue boils it all in the porch cauldron and spoons it into the fisher, a sip at a time.
...Cold. Why's it cold?
You hold up the ember. The brew in the cup glows faintly, the way the pool glows.
Whatever heals is down there. It always was.
That's his debt paid. Yours is your own.

steps.objective: Bring what you found to Rue on the porch.
story: I found what the witches' brew needed, and the fisher sat up. Whatever heals in their pool lies down there, with the shard.

quests.summary: A fisher lies fevered on the witches' porch, and they have nothing left to brew with. Find what the brew needs round the black pool, with the ember held up.
quests.title: The Witches' Debt

road.text: Someone's walked in your smoke since my first camp. Don't look round.

steps.awake: Not yet. Sit by the fire a while.

choices.reply: Names are for people who stay.
choices.story: She wouldn't give her name. Names are for people who stay, she said.

choices.reply: Someone had to. You walk like he did, and he forgot to eat.
choices.story: She was the one who left the bread at his first camp.
choices.text: You left the bread at his camp.

choices.reply: I'm going. I only came to see who carries it now.
choices.story: I told her to get away from our fire. She went.

done.text: Eat. You walk further on bread.
She sets a loaf on the log beside her and stands.
The fire gusts. Smoke rolls over the circle, and when it thins she is gone.
The loaf is still on the log, dark and round.

lines.text: Someone walks out of the dark and sits down across the fire. A grey hood, a grey coat, an eye stitched over the heart.
Gazebound. At my fire.
Hob gets up with his hammer in his fist. Nobody else moves.
So he's dead. I knew his smoke before I knew your face.

steps.objective: Sit at the caravan's fire.

people.maren: A hooded woman in Gazebound grey. She knew the stranger's smoke, and that he was dead. She left us bread.

story: A woman in Gazebound grey walked out of the dark and sat down at our fire. She knew the stranger's smoke, and that he was dead. Then she was gone in the smoke, and left a loaf behind.

steps.awake: Not yet. Her bread is still on the log.

choices.reply: You break it and eat. It's good bread, dark and sweet, an open eye pressed into the crust.
choices.story: I ate her bread. It was good.

choices.reply: You wrap it in a cloth for the road.

reward.claimed: You pack the loaf. It still smells of the fire.

items.name: Her Bread
items.tooltip: Dark and sweet, an open eye pressed into the crust. She left it at our fire.

reward.text: the loaf the hooded woman left on the log.
reward.title: Her Bread

choices.story: I kept her bread for the road.

choices.reply: Waste.
choices.story: I gave her bread to the fire. The stranger called it a waste.

lines.text: Eat it. Don't follow her.

steps.objective: Decide what to do with her bread: press an answer's number.

steps.awake: Not yet. Corin's watching you from his tent.

lines.text: She saw my tent. She let me be.
...Don't ask me who she is.

steps.objective: Talk to Corin, by his tent at the edge of the camp.

people.corin: He knows the hooded woman, and won't say who she is, as he won't say the stranger's name.

story: Corin knows her. He won't say who she is.

quests.summary: The voice says someone has walked in your smoke since his first camp. Sit at the caravan's fire tonight.
quests.title: The Hooded Traveller

clues.text: A tin box under the stones. Inside, a coal no bigger than a thumb, black and cold. An ember, gone out.
A journal, swollen with rain. It is signed with a circle cut through by a line: the mark from the tunnels.
Something heavy in old cloth: a carved stone, cut down to fit a pack. It hums faintly at your touch.

done.text: The journal's last page reads: "One more winter here. The ember is so small now. I'll walk in spring."
They didn't. Spring doesn't come for someone who stops. Take the stone. They'd want it walked.

steps.objective: Search the old camp: {found}/{needed}.

reward.claimed: You wrap the stone in its cloth again and pack it, with the journal.
reward.text: a stone of one's own, cut down to fit a pack, and the journal it was left with.
reward.title: Their Stone

story: In an old camp by the road I found another Wayfarer's ember, gone out, and their journal. They stopped walking, and their ember went home. They left their stone. I carry it now.

words.stone: A stone of my own, cut down to fit a pack. Set down and touched, it folds me back to it from any waystone I've touched, and the ember burns the walk it saves.

quests.summary: An old camp by the road, and the voice wants me to look at it. Somebody sat there too long.
quests.title: The Cache

done.text: She's mine? She's really mine?
Bramble. Her name's Bramble.
Pip leads Bramble to Agna's tent, and Agna pretends not to smile.

lines.text: In the stories every Wayfarer has a horse. Find me one? A brown one.

steps.name: Bramble
steps.objective: Find Pip a horse and bring it to the caravan's fire.

people.pip: Pip wanted a horse, like the Wayfarers in the stories. I found one, and Pip called her Bramble.

story: I brought Pip a horse. Pip called her Bramble, and she grazes by Agna's tent now.

quests.summary: Pip wants a horse, like the Wayfarers in the stories. Any horse will do, Pip says, as long as it's brown.
quests.title: The Road
